Subject: Chat streaming intermittently slow (us-west-2)

Hi Marissa / team,

We're seeing a spike in response times for our streaming chat sessions (user-facing). For the last 45 minutes, token delivery for streaming responses has been taking ~3-8s per token intermittently; end-to-end generation latency is ~6-12s longer than usual. This started around 08:20 PDT and affects ~20% of sessions in us-west-2.

Example: request id hippo-20260328-001 attached in case you need headers.

Can you confirm if this is a known incident and share recommended temporary workarounds while you investigate? This is impacting a scheduled demo in 90 minutes.

Thanks,
Claire

Date: 2026-03-28T09:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Chat streaming intermittently slow (us-west-2) — preliminary triage

Quick summary from infra triage:
- Observed symptom: intermittent per-token latency spikes for streaming endpoints (redwood-chat/stream) originating from a subset of GPU hosts in us-west-2.
- Probable cause (prelim): network bandwidth contention combined with an autoscaler race that caused several streaming workers to drop back to a CPU fallback path, which increases per-token wall time.
- Scope: ~15–25% of streaming sessions in us-west-2 between 08:15–09:10 PDT. Non-streaming batch/generate endpoints largely unaffected.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations we recommend:
1) If acceptable for the demo, switch to non-streaming generate endpoint (text.generate) — this avoids per-token delivery and will typically finish faster overall for short responses.
2) Temporarily pin to lower-latency model variant: redwood-medium-v2 (reduced context but faster tokens).
3) Reduce max_tokens and encourage using shorter top_p/temperature to lower token count.
4) Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes if you can (this reduces repeated computation).
5) Route traffic to another region if you have multi-region traffic (us-east-1) — we can whitelist and help with routing.

Longer-term fix: we've pushed a routing hotfix (reroute streaming traffic off saturated hosts) and increased streaming worker pool in us-west-2; both changes are already rolling. We'll monitor for recovery and share when the incident is resolved.

I'll prepare an abridged customer note you can send now.
—Hannah
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Chat streaming intermittently slow (us-west-2)

Hi Claire — quick update and immediate guidance.

Thanks again for reporting — we identified intermittent token delivery slowdowns originating from a subset of streaming hosts in us-west-2 and have already rolled two mitigations: a routing hotfix to avoid the saturated hosts and a temporary increase in streaming worker capacity. We're actively monitoring.

If you need an immediate workaround for your demo, here are concrete options (choose one):
- Option A (recommended for short responses): Switch to the non-streaming text.generate endpoint for your demo requests. Example: POST /v1/generate with the same prompt & reduced max_tokens=150. This avoids per-token streaming latency and often completes sooner for short outputs.
- Option B (keep streaming): Pin to redwood-medium-v2 and set max_tokens=120 and token_timeout_ms=10000. This reduces per-token compute and lowers the chance of hitting fallback paths.
- Option C (regional failover): Route demo traffic to us-east-1; we can add routing rules for your account in 10–15 minutes.

We apologize for the disruption. I've attached a one-page workaround playbook with command snippets. Please tell us which option you'd like and we will apply any routing or account changes immediately.

Subject: Incident follow-up and next steps — us-west-2 streaming latency (draft postmortem)

Hi Claire — quick follow-up with status and next steps.

Recovery: Our routing hotfix and worker scaling completed by 15:10 PDT on 2026-03-28; we saw client-facing recovery within ~20 minutes after that window.

Root cause (brief): A transient autoscaler race caused several streaming pods on a small subset of GPU hosts to drop into a CPU fallback path while network egress contention amplified per-token latency. We are preparing a full RCA with timeline.

What we've done for you:
- Applied a temporary routing override for your account to avoid the affected host pool.
- Shared a workaround playbook and assisted with a short-term region failover during your demo.
- Logged a support ticket for credits related to the incident; our CS team will propose a goodwill credit in the next 48 hours.

Next steps:
1) Draft postmortem is here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB2cPostmortemDraft (you have view/comment).
2) We'll publish a public postmortem on the status page after internal review.
3) Engineering will push a permanent fix to the autoscaler/routing logic in the next sprint; I'll share the rollout plan once scheduled.

If you have any additional impact details (e.g., specific user IDs, missed SLA windows), please attach them and we'll include them in the customer impact section.

Apologies again for the disruption — please let me know if you want a short call to walk through the postmortem.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Customer Success
